## TL;DR

This resumed turn did not change application source or repeat the macOS device workflow. I inspected the latest review finding and the existing QA record, confirmed that signed-in Projects and Tasks are still unverified and assigned to held human follow-up #1174, and ran the required scoped RepoOS check against the current branch. The check passed. I am not claiming the full task acceptance criteria are complete: #1174 has no recorded result, so this task still needs human evidence before it can be signed off.

## Work and rationale

The recovery prompt described #1169 as active, but both the branch task file and the RepoOS board initially showed it in review. The handoff status was superseded and no validation process was running. Since the current review finding required more work and the branch had no active review lock, I used the RepoOS CLI to return the task to active before continuing. This restored the status needed to run a fresh check and prepare an updated report draft.

I read the task specification, the QA record, the latest stored review report, and the current round report. Review pass 5 said that acceptance coverage remained incomplete because the Projects and Tasks screens had not been reached after sign-in. The latest engineering report also did not match the present source tree, which is why this draft records the current resumed session rather than reusing its narrative. The prior review is not treated as current approval.

The QA record describes the earlier macOS work: Xcode build with signing disabled and task-local DerivedData, LaunchServices launch with isolated Hub support storage, first-run rendering, discovery and addition of a live local server, and display of the sign-in page. It also documents the XCTest test-host registry write that was found and fixed with isolated temporary support storage and cleanup coverage. I did not repeat those macOS actions in this resumed turn, so these are cited as existing recorded evidence, not new observations made now.

The remaining authenticated screen check requires a human to complete the email-code sign-in and observe Projects and Tasks. Held task #1174 is now the designated follow-up. I retained the explicit not-verified status in the task notes and QA record. Its absence of results means the app's signed-in acceptance criterion remains outstanding; no evidence was invented to close it.

## Approaches tried

I first checked the branch and RepoOS state, then queried the handoff status and landability. RepoOS reported a superseded handoff with no live process and a stale review verdict. I returned the task to active using the RepoOS CLI so that the required validation could be run on this tree.

I ran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. The incremental remote bundle could not be applied because its mirror lacked the referenced base, and RepoOS automatically retried with a full bundle. The remote runner then verified the checked-out commit, installed dependencies, built the application, ran the changed-path test selection and browser gate, and returned success. Local formatting, lint, build freshness, branch-artifact and task-asset checks also passed, as did the UI smoke test. The test step was correctly skipped locally because the selected suite had already run on the remote validation host.

## Challenges and blockers

The only acceptance blocker is the missing human sign-in result. The email-code automation did not reach the signed-in web UI in the earlier QA run, and this turn did not have a human-provided result from #1174. The task therefore cannot honestly be described as fully verified, even though the scoped engineering check is green.

There was also an initial remote bundle transport mismatch. RepoOS recovered by transferring full history and completed validation successfully; there is no remaining check failure from that issue.

## Key learnings

A green scoped software check establishes that the current branch passes its configured changed-path validation. It does not substitute for a human-only authenticated product flow. Keep the projects/tasks acceptance item open until #1174 records observations for this build.

A superseded handoff is not proof that a task is actively being checked. Confirm the task status, handoff status, and review freshness before resuming; then use RepoOS status commands to restore the correct state. Finally, engineering report narratives need to match the current session and tree rather than relying on older generated rounds.
